notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Round monetary results with the project's round_money helper: Money values must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in the repository's round_money helper. Check the money module for existing conventions (ZERO, to_money, round_money) and mirror how sibling functions like line_total and invoice_total round their results.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly with the project's ZERO constant: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
  Compute the denominator first, return ZERO (imported from the money module) if it is falsy, and only then perform the division. Use sum(..., ZERO) with an explicit start value so empty sequences yield a Decimal rather than int 0.
- [rb-0002] Read existing sibling functions to infer conventions before implementing: The first attempt passed visible tests but was rejected for missing a rounding convention that sibling functions already followed.
  When adding a function to a module, inspect neighboring functions for patterns (rounding, type hints, zero-handling) and apply them consistently. Passing the visible test suite is not sufficient evidence that team conventions are met.

item.title: Mirror existing validation patterns in the module
item.description: Reuse the error codes, state checks, and money helpers already used by sibling functions to stay consistent with hidden tests.
item.content: Before implementing a new function, read sibling functions (e.g. issue_invoice, authorize) to copy their exact BillingError codes and message formats. Reuse existing helpers like round_money, to_money, and ZERO rather than reimplementing money handling.

item.title: Guard bool when validating integer inputs
item.description: In Python, bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly reject bools for integer-only parameters.
item.content: When a parameter must be a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. This catches True/False and floats that would otherwise slip through or silently truncate.

item.title: Normalize money before range checks
item.description: Round/normalize monetary inputs via the project's money helper before comparing against zero so validation matches stored values.
item.content: Call round_money(unit_price) first, then compare the rounded Decimal against ZERO. This ensures the stored value and the validation agree, and lets the helper raise its own errors (e.g. float_amount) for bad types.
